extracted.intended_audience: authors, reviewers, editors, and the research community in the life and biomedical sciences
extracted.subtask_description: The page describes eLife's policies and standards for conducting peer review at the journal, including outputs, editorial decision-making, transparency practices, and limits on revision requests. It explains how reviews are produced and published under eLife's 'Publish, then Review' model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goals of peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: eLife aims to improve the speed, visibility and usefulness of peer review; the overall aim is to make peer review faster, fairer and more open.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eLife envisions a system in which the outputs of peer review are the primary way research is assessed, rather than journal title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual outputs: public reviews and detailed author feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: The editorial process produces two outputs: (i) public reviews designed to be posted alongside a preprint for the benefit of the community; (ii) detailed feedback on the manuscript for the authors, including requests for revisions and suggestions for improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See eLife's 'Peer Review: eLife implementing "Publish, then Review" model of publishing' for more on publishing public reviews alongside preprints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial decisions made by active researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: All decisions are made by editors who are active researchers in the life and biomedical sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision-makers are practising researchers, implying domain expertise and subject-matter competence in editorial judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: No artificial limits on publications or acceptance rates
rubrics_metrics.description: eLife does not artificially limit the number of articles it publishes and does not have a set acceptance rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy supports selection based on scientific merit rather than quotas or target acceptance percentages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion among editors and reviewers before decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors and reviewers discuss their reviews with each other before reaching a decision on a manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborative discussion among reviewers and editors is used to reach informed decisions rather than relying solely on independent reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit requests for extra experiments to essential and time-reasonable
rubrics_metrics.description: Extra experiments are only requested if they are essential and can be reasonably completed within about two months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limits burdens on authors and speeds the revision process by avoiding demands for non-essential or long-term additional work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish reviews, revision recommendations, and author responses with accepted manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: The public reviews, revision recommendations, and author responses are published with accepted manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Making these materials public increases transparency, visibility of the review process, and accountability of all parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use Journal Impact Factor for assessment; support DORA
rubrics_metrics.description: eLife does not support the Impact Factor and is a co-founder of the Declaration on Research Assessment (DORA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eLife promotes assessment practices that do not rely on journal-level metrics, in line with DORA principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide regularly updated editorial-process metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Regularly updated metrics relating to the eLife editorial process are made available (via the Author Guide).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publicly available metrics allow stakeholders to examine performance of the editorial and peer-review process over time.
